topic.title: Friends only at weddings and funerals
topic.claim: Your closest college friends now meet only at weddings and funerals, and you've quietly accepted that as staying in touch.
topic.moment: You hug a best friend at a shaadi, say 'we must do this more often', and both know the next time is someone else's big event.

turn.believed: You're still close; life just got busy for a while.
turn.actually: The friendship has shrunk to attendance. Big events are the only thing with enough force left to get you all in one room.

topic.because: Nobody wants to be the one who plans and chases, so everyone waits for an occasion that summons them. The event does the work the friendship stopped doing.
topic.payoff: If your only reunions need a wedding card or a condolence call, pick a random Tuesday and be the one who calls.
topic.behaviour: Old friend groups reunite only at weddings and funerals, calling it staying in touch.
topic.mechanism: Nobody initiates, so only big events have the pull to gather everyone.
topic.group: people in their 30s drifting from college friends
topic.send_to: the college friend you only meet at other people's weddings
topic.why_now: Wedding season is when this quietly dawns on people.

score.why: The 'we must do this more often' hug at a wedding is lived by almost everyone; the turn that the event is doing the work the friendship stopped doing stings exactly right, no household trope involved.
